candidates.title: plannedTasks' materialised-tasks branch is never verified
candidates.detail: plannedTasks(bdir, st) short-circuits to 0 when len(st.Tasks) > 0 (cmd_status.go:178-180), which is exactly the state a normal run is in once it leaves the plan phase (plan.index.json is never deleted after materialiseTasks, so it still sits on disk in execute/finish phase). No test in this diff or pre-existing exercises this branch with an assertion on the tasks/planned output: the new TestStatusPlanPhaseSaysPlannedAndConfirmedClauses only covers the plan-phase case (st.Tasks empty, index present, planned=4); the pre-existing reviewerRun fixture (record_reviewer_test.go:23-49) does set st.Tasks non-empty alongside a real plan.index.json and is used by status tests such as TestStatusInternalReviewSkipped/TestStatusInternalReviewZeroCandidatesNotVerifyPending, but those tests never assert on the 'tasks' or 'planned' fields — so they exercise the line without verifying it. If the early return were dropped (e.g. plannedTasks always parsed the index and returned len(idx.Tasks) whenever it succeeded), every execute/finish-phase status call for a run whose plan.index.json is still on disk would wrongly report 'N planned (not yet materialised)' instead of real task counts, and no test would fail.

candidates.title: bundleHint assumes the created-branch convention, ignoring the adopted-branch rule documented next to it
candidates.detail: bundleHint's only positive branch guess is `"takt/"+slug` (select.go:122-123), and its doc comment states flatly that `takt init` commits the bundle on takt/<slug>. But cmd_init.go's chooseBranch (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:204-206, spec D9) documents two branch outcomes: on the default branch init creates takt/<slug>, but on any other branch init adopts the current branch (bi.adopted=true) and commits the bundle there instead — under whatever name that branch has, not takt/<slug>. For a run initialised via the adopted path, switching away from that branch and running `status`/`unlock` will fail loadBundle with fs.ErrNotExist, bundleHint's BranchExists(ctx, "takt/"+slug) check will correctly return false (no such branch was ever created), and the code falls through to "no run named <slug> under <base>; check the slug or pass --dir" — telling the user no such run exists when it does, just on a differently-named adopted branch. No existing helper maps a slug back to its actual (possibly adopted) branch, so this is a real gap between the new hint logic and the branch rule the surrounding code already knows about, not just an untested edge case.

verdicts.evidence: bundleHint's only positive guess is the created-branch name: `if exists, berr := ws.Repo.BranchExists(ctx, "takt/"+slug); berr == nil && exists { return "the run's bundle lives on branch takt/" + slug + "; check it out, or pass --dir" }` followed by a fallback claiming no such run exists (internal/cli/select.go:118-126). chooseBranch confirms the adopted path is real and produces a different branch name: `if cur != def { return &branchInit{branch: cur, def: def, adopted: true}, 0 }` (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:216-217), and cmdInit commits the bundle on `bi.branch` via commitInitBundle (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:116), i.e. on `cur`, not on `takt/<slug>`. For an adopted run, no `takt/<slug>` branch is ever created, so BranchExists there is false and bundleHint falls through to 'no run named <slug> under <base>' even though the run exists on the adopted branch. The diff's own new tests (TestStatusHintsAtTheBranchHoldingTheBundle, cmd_status_test.go:540, and TestUnlockHintsAtTheBranchHoldingTheBundle, cmd_unlock_test.go:14) only exercise the default-branch/created-branch case (`init` then `checkout main`), never the adopted-branch case, and no helper in the codebase maps a slug back to an actual adopted branch name.
